newsitem.title: CHINA: Post-handover China, HK stats to stay separate.
newsitem.headline: Post-handover China, HK stats to stay separate.

text.p: China's economic indicators will not include figures for Hong Kong in the first few years after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, a senior government statistician said on Friday.

Economic indicators, including Gross Domestic Product (GDP), inflation and industrial output, as well as foreign exchange reserves would not include figures for the territory after the handover, Qiu Xiaohua, chief economist of the State Statistical Bureau, told reporters.
"In future, figures such as GDP will include Hong Kong's only after convertibility (of the Chinese yuan) is resolved," Qiu said. He declined to comment further.

China announced in December 1996 that its yuan currency had become convertible on the current account. Officials have said they would like to see the yuan convertible on the capital account by the year 2000.
